strongest_angle: Examining how educator Arleen Lorrance created the popular phrase often attributed to Mahatma Gandhi, exploring the 1974 book chapter where it first appeared and how attribution shifted over time.

key_facts.fact: Mahatma Gandhi never said or wrote the quote 'be the change,' despite extensive digitization of his thousands of pages of material.
Educator Arleen Lorrance is credited by contemporary researchers and Quote Investigator with originating the phrase in a 1974 book chapter after working at a high school in Brooklyn, New York.
Mahatma Gandhi died in the year 1948, which is many years before the earliest close match of the quote appeared in print.
Author Benoit Denizet-Lewis met Arleen Lorrance, described as an octogenarian, to research the misattributed origins of the popular slogan for Literary Hub.
